leads.title: In the matter between: LETSWELETSE MOTSHIDIEMANG and ATTORNEY GENERAL - High Court judgement
leads.documents: Unanimous 11 June 2019 High Court ruling declaring Penal Code section 164 unconstitutional, decriminalizing same-sex sexual acts; includes Section 3 Constitution interpretation that 'sex' includes sexual orientation and quotes on dignity.
leads.detail: External links entry: 'In the matter between: LETSWELETSE MOTSHIDIEMANG and ATTORNEY GENERAL; the High Court judgement which decriminalised same-sex sexual activity in Botswana Archived 4 April 2022 at the Wayback Machine' - no direct URL visible in text

leads.title: Botswana Court of Appeal ruling - 29 November 2021
leads.documents: Unanimous rejection of Attorney-General appeal upholding 2019 decriminalization; holds laws criminalizing same-sex relations have outlived usefulness, with opinion by President Ian Kirby.
leads.detail: Cited in text as Court of Appeal decision 29 November 2021, retiring president Ian Kirby writing; Attorney-General Abraham Keetshabe appeal July 2019 noted - no URL visible

leads.title: Rectification of the Laws (Penal Code) Order, 2026 under Revision of the Laws Act
leads.documents: Formal March 2026 deletion of paragraphs (a) and (c) of Penal Code section 164 from statute book after years of legislative inaction following 2019 and 2021 court invalidation.
leads.detail: Cited as statutory instrument titled 'Rectification of the Laws (Penal Code) Order, 2026', made by Law Revision Commissioner - no URL visible

leads.title: Penal Code Sections 164(a) and 167
leads.documents: Colonial-era provisions challenged as unconstitutional for interfering with liberty, privacy and bodily autonomy; previously criminalized sodomy/unnatural acts up to seven years, applied to men and later women.
leads.detail: Cited as Section 164(a) and 167 Penal Code, lead plaintiff Letsweletse Motshidiemang, LEGABIBO as amicus Nov 2017 - no URL visible

leads.title: Employment Act 1982
leads.documents: Ban on employment discrimination on basis of sexual orientation since 2010, making Botswana one of few African countries with such protections.
leads.detail: Cited as 'The Employment Act 1982 (Tswana: Molao wa Thapo 1982)' - no URL visible

leads.title: Botswana High Court September 2017 transgender gender-marker ruling
leads.documents: Ruling that Registrar of National Registration refusal to change transgender man's gender marker was unreasonable and violated rights to dignity, privacy, expression, equal protection, non-discrimination and freedom from inhumane treatment; government complied with new ID after dropping appeal.
leads.detail: Cited as September 2017 High Court ruling, government announced then dropped appeal in December - no URL visible

leads.title: Botswana High Court December 2017 - Ricki Kgositau ruling
leads.documents: Ruling that Government must recognise activist and transgender woman Ricki Kgositau's gender identity as female, companion to Sept 2017 precedent on legal gender change.
leads.detail: Cited as December 2017 hearing/ruling for Ricki Kgositau - no URL visible

leads.title: LEGABIBO registration litigation - High Court November 2014 and Court of Appeal 16 March 2016
leads.documents: Rights machinery precedent: High Court ordered Government to register main LGBTQ organisation LEGABIBO; Court of Appeal unanimously held refusal unlawful, enabling offices and Drop In Centres.
leads.detail: Cited as 2013 suit by 14 LeGaBiBo members via Unity Dow, High Court Nov 2014 ruling, Court of Appeal 16 March 2016 ruling; registrar rationale quoted - no URL visible

leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2011 Human Rights Report - Botswana
leads.documents: Documents enforcement climate: no law explicitly criminalizing consensual same-sex activity but 'unnatural acts' criminalized and believed directed at LGBT persons; police did not target same-sex activity, no reports of violence based on orientation/gender identity that year.
leads.detail: Cited as 'U.S. Department of State's 2011 Human Rights Report' - no URL visible

leads.title: UK government travel advice for Botswana: Local laws and customs / Asylumlaw.org Sexual Minorities & HIV Status (Botswana)
leads.documents: Institutional visitor-safety and asylum-use packets on local laws/customs and sexual minorities/HIV status used for asylum purposes; plus LEGABIBO official website for in-country support.
